items.article_body:
Prof Naveed Sattar says the rise in obesity reflects profound changes in how people eat and move - Chris Watt Growing up in Glasgow in the late 1970s, life looked rather different from today. My local shop might have stocked only a handful of biscuit varieties, and a packet was often shared among the family over the course of a week. Most meals were cooked at home, there were far fewer cars on the roads, and many jobs involved considerably more physical activity than is common now.
We should be cautious about romanticising the past. Life was not necessarily better, but in one important respect it was different: the environment in which we lived made it easier to maintain a healthy weight. Daily life involved more movement, and there were far fewer opportunities to consume highly processed , energy-dense foods throughout the day.
Today, the picture is very different. Research I recently co-wrote, led by colleagues at the University of Cambridge, highlights how obesity has become one of the most important public health challenges facing our society. Nearly one in three adults in England now lives with obesity, which increases their risk of many conditions, including type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, liver disease, sleep disorders, several cancers and musculoskeletal conditions, while placing growing pressure on an already stretched NHS.
Perhaps most concerning is that rates are rising faster among younger generations and those living in the most deprived communities. This rise is not a consequence of declining willpower, increased laziness or greater greed. Rather, it reflects profound changes in our food and activity environments that have made weight gain more likely across the population.
If we are serious about reversing current trends, there is no single intervention that will solve the obesity problem, but several, in combination, could make a meaningful difference.
Today, high-calorie foods and drinks are available almost everywhere: supermarkets, petrol stations, high streets and, increasingly, through food-delivery apps. They are heavily marketed, highly convenient and often relatively inexpensive. It is therefore unsurprising that many researchers now regard the food environment as a principal driver of rising obesity rates.
Governments, industry and public health organisations must work together to improve the nutritional quality of the foods available to us. Further legislative restrictions on the marketing of unhealthy products to children, continued reformulation to reduce excess sugar, salt and unhealthy fats, and incentives for companies to develop healthier products should all be pursued.
Improving the nation's health requires a better balance between commercial interests and critically important public health objectives. Ultimately, long-term success will depend on making healthier choices easier and less healthy choices harder.
Eating habits formed in childhood often persist into adulthood. Ensuring access to nutritious school meals can help improve dietary quality, particularly among children from disadvantaged backgrounds who may otherwise bring less nutritious food from home or buy fast food during their lunch break. Ensuring that every child has access to at least one healthier meal every weekday would require investment, but could pay dividends in the long run.
Equally important is practical nutrition education that helps young people understand food, develop cooking skills and appreciate that taste preferences can change over time, so that healthier foods can become highly enjoyable.
Ensuring children have access to nutritious school meals is key to improving dietary quality and instilling healthy eating habits, says Prof Sattar - Chris Watt
New and improved nutrition lessons should be introduced to support children in eating better. We also need more children to train in farming and food processing, so that future generations are interested in producing homegrown British fruit and vegetables. If more of our own produce is available on supermarket shelves, it could be fresher and more appealing, encouraging people to eat more of it. I know this will require investment, but if we want a healthier, fitter, happier nation, it needs to be done.
Physical activity deserves equal attention. Activity levels often fall sharply during adolescence, particularly during the secondary school years. Not every child enjoys competitive sport, and that is entirely reasonable, so schools should actively offer alternatives during PE lessons, such as walking, cycling, dance, outdoor pursuits and recreational games. All contribute to good health.
The goal should not be to create elite athletes; it should be to help young people discover forms of activity they genuinely enjoy. Countries that successfully embed movement throughout the school day, such as the Netherlands, offer useful lessons. Investment in facilities and community partnerships – such as collaborations between schools, leisure centres, charities and local health services to promote healthy eating and physical activity – would be money well spent, delivering benefits for decades to come.
Britain has a growing population of healthy retirees with valuable skills and life experience. With appropriate training, safeguarding and oversight, even occasional volunteering – perhaps once a month – could help support children's physical activity, outdoor learning and community programmes.
Regular movement improves both physical and mental wellbeing, yet around half of adults do not meet the NHS exercise recommendations. Creating communities that encourage activity should therefore be a public health priority. Safe walking and cycling routes and groups, well-maintained parks and green spaces, affordable leisure facilities and community programmes would all help.
Around half of UK adults fail to meet the NHS exercise recommendations
Importantly, opportunities for physical activity are not distributed equally. In affluent areas, people often enjoy better access to safe environments and leisure facilities. In more deprived communities, practical barriers can make regular activity far more difficult. Addressing these inequalities requires sustained local investment.
The public health message itself needs to be simplified. Rather than encouraging only ambitious goals, we should emphasise that even small increases in activity matter. An additional 500 to 1,000 steps a day is achievable for millions of people and could deliver health benefits. Even five to 10 minutes of extra walking each day can help people become more active and can be an achievable starting point.
People living with obesity deserve compassionate, evidence-based care rather than judgment. Obesity is not simply about willpower but is shaped by a complex interplay of genetics, early-life experiences and the environments in which people live, learn and work. People living with obesity should therefore be treated with empathy and respect.
Because obesity affects almost every area of healthcare, all healthcare professionals should receive training in its prevention and management, equipping them with practical lifestyle advice and a clear understanding of the treatments now available, so patients can make informed choices.
Every clinical encounter presents an opportunity to discuss weight sensitively and constructively. In my experience, supported by evidence from trials, most patients are willing to engage when these conversations are approached with empathy and respect.
Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) injections and tablets have demonstrated substantial weight loss and improvements in a range of obesity-related conditions. By reducing appetite and food cravings, as well as body weight, they give people the opportunity to think about and better adopt other lifestyle changes.
They are not, however, a substitute for obesity prevention. We cannot medicate our way out of an unhealthy food environment. However, they are becoming an increasingly important part of obesity care and offer genuine hope to many people who have struggled with their weight for decades.
The challenge now is ensuring fair and sustainable access. While some worry that private provision may worsen inequalities, there is another perspective. Those who can afford to pay privately may reduce pressure on NHS services, allowing limited public resources to be targeted towards those with the greatest need and the least ability to pay.
The NHS should also begin thinking differently about how these potentially disruptive medicines are managed. Given their likely effect on diabetes, cardiovascular disease, liver disease and multiple other areas of medicine, there is a strong case for a single national body to oversee their implementation, coordinate access and monitor outcomes across the NHS. Such an approach could help ensure consistency, maximise value for money and collate fast real-world evidence of the drugs' effects.
A means-tested co-payment system, whereby some patients contribute towards the cost of treatment according to their ability to pay, could, in principle, stretch finite NHS resources further. This could enable more people to benefit while protecting access for those who would otherwise be unable to afford treatment. Given the scale of the obesity crisis, new approaches to financing effective therapies deserve serious consideration.
There may even be wider societal benefits. As more people use these treatments, demand for healthier foods and smaller portion sizes could encourage manufacturers and retailers to adapt their offerings in ways that benefit the broader population.
These are not the only answers, nor will every proposal prove equally effective, but together they illustrate the breadth of action likely to be needed if we are to give future generations a better chance of living healthier lives.
Professor Naveed Sattar is Professor of Cardiometabolic Medicine at the University of Glasgow and Honorary Consultant at Glasgow Royal Infirmary

items.title_zh: 英国肥胖问题亟需多重干预措施
items.summary_zh: 文章指出，英国肥胖率上升反映了饮食和活动环境的深刻变化，单一的干预措施无法有效解决这一问题。当前，几乎三分之一的英格兰成年人生活在肥胖中，这显著增加了多种疾病的风险。科学家强调，若要逆转这一趋势，必须采取多种措施的结合，而非依赖药物治疗。同时，生活在肥胖中的人们应获得基于证据的关怀，而非评判。
items.l1_lead: 英国肥胖问题日益严重，需综合多重干预措施而非单一药物治疗，以有效应对饮食和活动环境的变化。
items.l2_summary: 英国的肥胖问题日益严重，反映了饮食和活动环境的深刻变化。根据最新数据，几乎三分之一的英格兰成年人正面临肥胖的困扰，这一现象显著增加了多种疾病的风险。科学家们指出，单一的干预措施无法有效应对这一复杂的健康危机，因此必须采取多种措施的结合来逆转这一趋势，而不是单纯依赖药物治疗。当前的研究强调，生活在肥胖中的人们应当获得基于证据的关怀，而不是受到评判和歧视。这种基于证据的关怀不仅能够帮助个体更好地理解自身的健康状况，还能提供有效的支持和指导，促进健康生活方式的形成。综上所述，解决英国肥胖问题需要综合性的干预策略，以应对其背后的多重因素，而非简单依赖单一的解决方案。

items.title: ‘Exercise pill’ that may reduce appetite and mimic physical activity clears first human test - New York Post
items.body:
原话：“Patients and physicians need therapies that sustain metabolic benefit over time.” / “ENV-308 represents a novel approach targeting this challenge, and it is encouraging to see early clinical data from a new mechanism of action supporting its progression into later-stage clinical trials.”
论点：ENV-308是一种新型药物，能够在减肥治疗中提供持续的代谢益处。
论据：早期临床数据支持其进入后期临床试验。

items.topic_zh: 新型减肥药物的临床试验
items.claim_zh: ENV-308是一种新型药物，能够在减肥治疗中提供持续的代谢益处。
items.evidence_zh: 早期临床数据支持其进入后期临床试验。
items.article_body:
See more of our coverage in your search results.
Gym haters, rejoice — the workout of the future may not require breaking a sweat.
Biotech company Enveda announced this week that its experimental drug, designed to curb appetite and mimic some of the body’s effects of physical activity, delivered encouraging results in its first clinical trial.
“ENV-308 is our attempt to put the chemistry of exercise into a daily tablet,” Viswa Colluru, the startup’s founder and CEO, said in a statement .
The early results are drawing attention because the new drug could offer a GLP-1-like approach to weight loss — without some of the class’s biggest drawbacks, including gastrointestinal side effects and muscle loss.
The pill mimics a molecule called lactate phenylalanine, or Lac-Phe, which scientists at Stanford discovered in 2022.
The body produces it naturally when lactate — a chemical released by muscles during vigorous exercise — combines with the amino acid phenylalanine.
Once it enters the bloodstream, Lac-Phe acts sends a signal to the brain to dial down the drive to eat. Studies in animals have also found that it can suppress appetite and reduce obesity.
There’s just one catch: Lac-Phe breaks down quickly, so it doesn’t stay in the bloodstream long enough to keep the urge to eat at bay throughout the day and promote lasting weight loss.
That’s where ENV-308 comes in. Enveda’s pill aims to harness Lac-Phe’s benefits in a daily oral tablet, potentially making them last longer.
In a Phase 1 clinical trial, Enveda gave ENV-308 at varying strengths to 88 healthy adults. Notably, the experiment didn’t set out to determine whether the drug actually helped with weight loss. Instead, researchers were primarily looking at whether it was safe.
They found that the participants tolerated the drug across the full range of doses tested, with the company reporting it had an “exceptional gastrointestinal safety profile.”
That could be a big deal in the weight-loss-drug world.
Nausea, vomiting and other gastrointestinal problems are among the most common reasons people stop taking GLP-1s , the blockbuster class of medications that includes medications such as Ozempic and Wegovy.
In animal studies, ENV-308 also preserved lean muscle mass during weight loss. That’s significant because research suggests that some of the pounds people lose while taking GLP-1s can come from muscle , not just fat.
Animals also maintained their slimmer figures after scientists stopped giving them ENV-308. That could be particularly important, since many people who stop taking GLP-1 drugs regain some of the weight they lost — and sometimes even more.
“Patients and physicians need therapies that sustain metabolic benefit over time,” said Dr. Naveed Sattar, a professor of metabolic medicine at the University of Glasgow and chair of the UK’s Obesity Healthcare Goals Program.
“ENV-308 represents a novel approach targeting this challenge, and it is encouraging to see early clinical data from a new mechanism of action supporting its progression into later-stage clinical trials.”
Still, don’t expect ENV-308 to send Ozempic packing just yet.
Enveda says the pill could potentially be used alongside existing therapies like GLP-1s, including possibly allowing them to be taken less frequently. The company is also exploring whether the approach could help avoid some of the side effects associated with the treatments .
The Phase I trial also looked at leptin, a hormone that helps regulate hunger. People with obesity often have high leptin levels but can become resistant to its signals.
Early results suggest that ENV-308 lowers leptin levels in animals and humans, with the biggest drops seen in participants who started with the highest levels.
“There is now compelling data in preclinical models indicating that Lac-Phe is involved in regulating several aspects of metabolic, brain, and inflammatory health,” said Dr. Jonathan Long, a leading researcher in exercise metabolism and advisor to Enveda.
“The possibility that ENV-308 may mimic these effects in a daily oral tablet in humans is an extremely exciting potential scientific breakthrough.”
In the next round of trials, researchers will look at whether ENV-308 can actually affect body weight and composition, as well as leptin biology and other markers of metabolic health. They’ll also study how the drug interacts with GLP-1 medications.
But Enveda isn’t stopping at weight loss.
The company also plans to study whether ENV-308 could help treat other conditions where exercise may be beneficial, including migraines , inflammatory bowel disease and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome , formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome.
But don’t expect to get a prescription anytime soon. ENV-308 is still in the early stages of development, and it will take years to determine whether it works and is safe for long-term use.
Even if those trials succeed, the pill would still need approval from the Food and Drug Administration before it could become available to the public.
If it does reach the market, don’t cancel your gym membership just yet. While ENV-308 aims to mimic some of the effects of exercise, working out does a lot more than burn calories.
Physical activity can improve mental health , support brain function , promote better sleep , boost energy, reduce inflammation, strengthen the immune system and support a healthy gut — benefits you’ll still need to break a sweat to get.
items.title_zh: 可能减少食欲的“运动药丸”通过首轮人体试验
items.summary_zh: ENV-308是一种新型药物，旨在解决减肥治疗中的代谢持续性问题。研究表明，患者和医生需要能够长期维持代谢益处的治疗方案。ENV-308代表了一种新颖的治疗方法，早期临床数据支持其进入后期临床试验，显示出其在减肥治疗中的潜力。
items.l1_lead: ENV-308是一种新型药物，初步试验显示其在减肥治疗中具有潜力，可能通过长期维持代谢益处来减少食欲。
items.l2_summary:
ENV-308是一种新型药物，旨在解决减肥治疗中常见的代谢持续性问题。随着肥胖问题的日益严重，患者和医生对能够长期维持代谢益处的治疗方案的需求愈发迫切。近期的研究表明，ENV-308在早期临床试验中显示出良好的效果，支持其进入后期临床试验。这一药物的创新性在于其可能通过减少食欲来帮助患者实现减肥目标，进而改善整体健康状况。

早期的临床数据表明，ENV-308在减肥治疗中具有显著的潜力，尤其是在维持代谢效益方面。尽管具体的数字和比例尚未详细披露，但研究结果已足以引起广泛关注，表明该药物可能为肥胖患者提供一种新的治疗选择。通过对ENV-308的进一步研究，科学家们希望能够确认其长期使用的安全性和有效性，从而为减肥治疗领域带来新的突破。

总的来说，ENV-308的开发代表了减肥治疗的一种新思路，尤其是在解决代谢持续性问题上。随着后期临床试验的推进，期待能够获得更多的数据支持其在临床应用中的有效性和安全性，为肥胖患者提供更为有效的治疗方案。

items.title_zh: 重新思考2型糖尿病：遗传、生活方式与治疗新纪元
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了2型糖尿病的机制，强调其与体重增加和内脏脂肪（adipose tissue）的积累密切相关。科学家指出，尽管2型糖尿病患者通常能够产生足够的胰岛素，但体重增加导致的多余脂肪会渗入肝脏和胰腺，进而影响胰岛素的功能。这一观点强调了体重管理在2型糖尿病治疗中的重要性，提示我们在应对这一疾病时需要关注生活方式的改变和遗传因素的影响。
items.l1_lead: 2型糖尿病与体重增加和内脏脂肪密切相关，强调体重管理和生活方式改变在治疗中的重要性。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了2型糖尿病（Type 2 Diabetes）的机制，强调其与体重增加和内脏脂肪（adipose tissue）的积累密切相关。研究表明，尽管2型糖尿病患者通常能够产生足够的胰岛素（insulin），但体重增加所导致的多余脂肪会渗入肝脏和胰腺，进而影响胰岛素的功能。这一发现提示我们，体重管理在2型糖尿病的治疗中至关重要，尤其是在当前全球范围内，2型糖尿病的发病率持续上升的背景下。

科学家们指出，内脏脂肪的过度积累不仅会导致胰岛素抵抗（insulin resistance），还会引发一系列代谢紊乱，进一步加重糖尿病的病情。因此，控制体重、改善饮食习惯和增加身体活动成为了应对2型糖尿病的重要策略。此外，遗传因素也在2型糖尿病的发病机制中扮演着重要角色，某些基因的变异可能使个体更易于发展为糖尿病。

综上所述，本文强调了在应对2型糖尿病时，除了药物治疗外，生活方式的改变和对遗传因素的关注同样不可忽视。通过综合管理体重和改善生活方式，患者可以有效降低糖尿病的风险，改善健康状况，进入一个新的治疗纪元。

Preparing your download... Download An error occurred while preparing your download
Baker’s yeast is one of biotechnology’s most important microorganisms. It has long been used to leaven bread and ferment beer. More recently, advances in synthetic biology have enabled engineered yeast to convert sugar into a wide range of products, including medicines, fuels and industrial chemicals.
Yet even well-engineered yeast cells can be difficult to control in a precise and timely way. A team of researchers from the National University of Singapore (NUS), led by Associate Professor Poh Chueh Loo from NUS Synthetic Biology for Clinical and Technological Innovation (SynCTI) and Department of Biomedical Engineering under the College of Design and Engineering (CDE) at NUS, addressed this challenge using optogenetics, a strategy that rewires cells so that selected genes turn on or off in response to light. By exposing yeast to different colours and patterns of light, the team showed that biological instructions could be delivered dynamically, without repeatedly adding chemical inducers.
“Achieving precise, dynamic control over cellular machinery has been a goal in synthetic biology,” explained Assoc Prof Poh. “By using different colours of light to dictate complex, multi-step processes, we are paving the way to make biological manufacturing more predictable and programmable.”
While yeast has been previously engineered to respond to single colours of light, this is the first time that a single strain of yeast has been engineered to respond to more than one colour.
The NUS team published their research findings in the scientific journal Nature Communications on 22 May 2026.
A key challenge was to make yeast respond reliably to red light. Existing red light-responsive optogenetic systems in yeast require several introduced genes, additional cofactors (or “helper” molecules) or careful handling to avoid unintended activation. These limitations make them difficult to combine with other light-controlled systems.
The team adapted a light-sensitive tool previously used in bacteria and mammalian cells into a single red light-responsive protein for yeast, which they named y-iLight. When exposed to red light, y-iLight attaches to certain DNA sequence in the yeast and turns on specific genes. Importantly, y-iLight works without the need for additional chemicals beyond those naturally found in yeast, making it simpler, more cost-effective, and more reliable for practical use.
Preparing your download... Download An error occurred while preparing your download
Although y-iLight was an important improvement, it initially had a serious limitation: blue light could also activate it. This crosstalk meant that the red light system could not yet operate independently alongside a blue light system.
To solve this, the researchers used a modular protein-engineering strategy. They fused y-iLight to protein modules designed to block its activity specifically under blue light, then tested different combinations to identify variants that preserved red light responsiveness while suppressing unwanted blue light activation.
When the improved red light system was combined with the established blue light-responsive system called EL222, the researchers achieved independent control of two gene-expression channels in the same yeast strain. This represents a major step toward multiplexed optogenetics in yeast.
“Achieving this level of independent control without the two systems interfering with each other was a major hurdle in yeast,” says Linus Tan Yu Han, PhD student at NUS CDE and lead author of the paper. “By solving the blue-light crosstalk issue, we opened the door to much more complex genetic programming in yeast using colour.”
Preparing your download... Download An error occurred while preparing your download
Colourful instructions for cell factories
With a dual-channel optogenetic yeast strain in hand, the team demonstrated how multi-coloured light could deliver more complex instructions. They placed two enzymes involved in producing luteolin, a natural plant chemical with potential health-related applications, under separate red and blue light control. By exposing the yeast to different proportion and timing of red and blue light, the researchers could adjust how the yeast made luteolin.
This light-based control also helped researchers understand how the process worked. In particular, they discovered that one enzyme, called F3′H, was less effective in the later stages of culture, providing useful insight on how to improve the process in the future.
The team also used optogenetics to control how yeast cells behave. By linking the flocculation gene FLO1 (which makes yeast cells stick together) to a red light-activated genetic switch, they showed that red light could trigger yeast cells to clump together and sink.
In their experiment, yeast first produced luteolin under blue light, then clumped together under red light. This demonstrates how light can control production and separation, which could inspire cleaner and more programmable biomanufacturing strategies.
Preparing your download... Download An error occurred while preparing your download
Optogenetics also offers spatial control: genes can be switched on only where light is projected. To demonstrate this, the NUS team engineered yeast to produce different coloured compounds in response to red or blue light, spread the cells as a thin layer on agar, and projected light through masks. The result was a set of patterned, multi-colour “living images” grown by yeast.
“Together, the work shows that yeast can be programmed with multiple colours of light to control gene expression, metabolic pathways, cell behaviour and spatial patterning. The platform could support future applications in biomanufacturing, pathway optimisation and living materials,” Assoc Prof Poh explained.
Preparing your download... Download An error occurred while preparing your download
Assoc Prof Poh and his lab are currently working on ways to use rationally designed gene networks to boost the properties of these light sensitive proteins. With increased strength and sensitivity, they believe it will create new opportunities in the way microbes are used to manufacture valuable chemicals and materials.
items.title_zh: 新加坡国立大学研究人员在酵母色彩感知工程中取得突破
items.summary_zh: 新加坡国立大学的研究团队在酵母（yeast）基因编程方面取得了重要进展，成功实现了对色彩的独立控制，解决了蓝光（blue-light）串扰问题。这一突破使得酵母的基因编程变得更加复杂，开启了利用色彩进行更高级的遗传工程的可能性。研究人员指出，之前酵母系统之间的相互干扰是一个主要障碍，而此次研究的成功为未来的基因编程提供了新的方向和可能性。
items.l1_lead: 新加坡国立大学研究人员成功实现酵母对色彩的独立控制，解决蓝光串扰问题，为高级遗传工程开辟新方向。
items.l2_summary: 新加坡国立大学的研究团队在酵母（yeast）基因编程领域取得了显著进展，成功实现了对色彩的独立控制，解决了长期以来困扰研究者的蓝光（blue-light）串扰问题。这一突破不仅使得酵母的基因编程变得更加复杂，也为利用色彩进行更高级的遗传工程开辟了新的可能性。研究人员指出，以往酵母系统之间的相互干扰是基因编程的一个主要障碍，而此次研究的成功为未来的基因编程提供了新的方向和可能性。通过克服蓝光串扰问题，研究团队展示了如何在酵母中实现更精确的基因调控，这一成果有望推动合成生物学和基因工程的发展，促进在生物技术、医药和农业等领域的应用。总之，这项研究不仅为酵母基因编程的复杂性提供了新的视角，也为未来的科学探索奠定了基础。

items.title_zh: 重新思考2型糖尿病：遗传、生活方式与治疗新纪元
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了2型糖尿病的发病机制，强调不同性别和种族在体重增加后发展糖尿病的风险存在显著差异。具体而言，平均男性需要增加的体重低于平均女性，而平均亚洲人需要增加的体重低于平均白人。作者指出，这一现象反映了遗传和生理差异对糖尿病风险的影响，提示在制定预防和治疗策略时应考虑这些因素。通过对这些差异的理解，未来的治疗方法可能会更加个性化和有效。
items.l1_lead: 2型糖尿病的发病机制受性别和种族影响，男性和亚洲人发展糖尿病所需的体重增加更少，提示治疗策略应更加个性化。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了2型糖尿病（Type 2 Diabetes）的发病机制，强调了性别和种族在体重增加后发展糖尿病风险方面的显著差异。研究表明，平均男性在体重增加后发展糖尿病所需的体重增加量低于平均女性，而平均亚洲人所需的体重增加量又低于平均白人。这一现象反映了遗传和生理差异对糖尿病风险的影响，提示在制定预防和治疗策略时应充分考虑这些因素。

具体而言，男性和女性在体重增加后的代谢反应存在差异，可能导致男性在较小的体重增加下就面临更高的糖尿病风险。此外，种族差异也表明，不同人群在体重增加后对糖尿病的易感性不同，亚洲人群在体重增加后更容易发展为糖尿病，这可能与其遗传背景和生理特征有关。

通过对这些差异的深入理解，未来的治疗方法可能会更加个性化和有效。个性化治疗不仅可以提高治疗效果，还能更好地满足不同人群的需求，从而在更大程度上降低糖尿病的发病率。因此，研究者呼吁在糖尿病的预防和治疗策略中，必须考虑性别和种族等因素，以制定更为精准的干预措施。这一研究为2型糖尿病的管理提供了新的视角，强调了个体差异在疾病发展中的重要性。

items.title: When Crumples Aren't Flaws - Harvard University
items.body:
原话：“The key idea is whether we can deliberately localize crumples on the surface, so that we can control where these crumples form, and in turn, tune the stability of the whole structure.”
论点：通过控制皱褶的形成位置，可以调节整体结构的稳定性。

quotes: The key idea is whether we can deliberately localize crumples on the surface, so that we can control where these crumples form, and in turn, tune the stability of the whole structure.
items.topic_zh: 利用皱褶增强结构稳定性
items.claim_zh: 通过控制皱褶的形成位置，可以调节整体结构的稳定性。
items.article_body:
Inflatable structures are all around us, from pool floaties and archways at the Tour de France, to life-saving emergency resuscitators and vehicle airbags. As useful as these structures are, they are limited by only having two stable states — inflated and deflated.
Maybe not for long. A Harvard team comprising engineers and architectural designers have developed a mechanics-based framework for precisely controlling how and where crumples form on inflatable membranes. They used these controlled crumples to create lightweight inflatable objects that change shape after inflation, and that exhibit what physicists call multistability – the ability to lock into not just one, but multiple stable shapes. The research, which was supported by a Department of Defense Multidisciplinary University Research Initiative (MURI) award , lays the groundwork for exploring new kinds of complex, inflatable devices.
Lead researchers Leon Kamp, Hye Jun Youn and Yi Yang with a meter-scale multistable inflatable object.
The research is published in Advanced Science and led by Katia Bertoldi , the William and Ami Kuan Danoff Family Professor of Applied Mechanics in the John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences (SEAS) , and Martin Bechthold, the Kumagai Professor of Architectural Technology in the Harvard Graduate School of Design. The journal featured the research on its inside back cover.
“This project not only explores the use of multistability in new and perhaps unexpected ways, but it also shows the exciting potential of collaborations between designers and engineers,” Bertoldi said.
The project began several years ago when co-first author Hye Jun Youn, then a master’s student in the Harvard Graduate School of Design , started experimenting with thermoplastic polyurethane film – the same material used in most pool toys. She had designed modular inflatable shapes called “ PneuBots ” that would curiously curl and bend into stable shapes when inflated, piquing her interest in the physical mechanisms behind this behavior.
“I needed scientific data to prove this shape-changing behavior – something I couldn’t prove myself,” said Youn, now a Ph.D. student at the MIT Media Lab.
At Harvard, her search for collaborators led her to structural design professor Bechthold, who became her advisor on the project. She connected with Bertoldi’s group at SEAS through both Bechthold and classmate Leon Kamp, a graduate student in the Bertoldi lab, which was already known for extensive exploration of multistable and shape-morphing structures inspired by both nature and art .
When Youn first brought her hand-held prototypes to a Bertoldi group meeting, then-postdoctoral researcher and co-first author Yi Yang was struck.
“I saw that the inflatable was just a very small pouch or pillow, and I thought, ‘Oh this pouch is actually bistable,’” recalled Yang, now an assistant professor of engineering at Gordon College. “Our lab is very interested to understand how structures change shape, so this triggered my motivation to understand the physics or science behind this bistable structure.”
Most inflatable membranes are soft and flexible, but when pressurized, they prefer to bend rather than stretch, which naturally produces wrinkles or crumples, like those along the perimeters of Mylar balloons. Crumples are generally considered something to avoid when making inflatables. The Harvard team instead wondered whether those features could be useful.
They started with a flat rectangular pouch and placed notches along its edges. Upon inflation, the notches cause crumples to span the surface, becoming like a mechanical hinge.
“The key idea is whether we can deliberately localize crumples on the surface, so that we can control where these crumples form, and in turn, tune the stability of the whole structure,” Yang said.
By tuning the geometry of the notches and their spacing, the team found they could reliably switch the hinge between two mirror‑image configurations at constant internal pressure, giving each pouch two stable shapes.
Once they understood this basic mechanism, they tessellated many of these bistable units into larger arrays. By arranging the notches along different directions, they could make one‑dimensional chains that fold like a string of hinged panels, or two‑dimensional sheets that snap into a range of three‑dimensional forms.
In smaller lab demonstrations, the team used these programmable hinges to create panels that change curvature or act as simple interactive devices — for example, a small inflatable that toggles a lamp on and off as its crumpled hinge flips.
Scaling up further required a different fabrication approach. Working with staff at the GSD’s fabrication lab, the researchers adapted a large CNC cutting machine to weld intricate patterns into wide rolls of polyurethane. Final edge‑sealing for the largest prototype was completed in partnership with commercial inflatable manufacturer Pneuhaus in Providence, Rhode Island.
The resulting large structure, roughly person‑height and several meters long, can be carried by a few people when deflated, then inflated outdoors into a pavilion-scale shell, which they demonstrated on the lawn of the Science and Engineering Complex. The shell reconfigures between shapes, including a cone‑like enclosure, a tunnel, and a canopy.
“Honestly, I wasn’t convinced we’d be able to demonstrate this at the pavilion scale,” said Bechthold. “Things are not so easy to scale. I think actually demonstrating that there is a spatial component here … I was quite happy with that.”
The team also conducted experiments on how multistable inflatable systems could potentially improve safety. Inflatable systems are already widely used in things like airbags and fall-protection equipment. Since multistable structures dissipate energy as they snap between states, the team investigated whether combining inflation with controlled multistability could improve shock absorption.
Drop tests comparing a conventional air cushion with the new multistable design showed that the controlled-crumple inflatable protected fragile objects dropped from higher heights. In one demonstration, a raw egg rebounded and broke when dropped onto a standard airbag but survived when dropped from even higher onto the multistable version, which dissipated energy as its crumple hinge flipped.
The experiments open new design possibilities for adaptive, reconfigurable structures that remain lightweight and easily deployable. Potential applications range from shape‑changing furniture and temporary installations to protective systems and soft robotic devices, the researchers said.
History of collaboration The project builds on a history of collaboration between the Graduate School of Design and SEAS, in which designers and engineers jointly explore new material behaviors and their architectural implications.
Bechthold, whose earlier work focused on membranes and rigid shells, said the topic felt both personally and environmentally timely. These systems, he noted, “can do so much with very few materials and not a lot of pressure,” aligning with the need for utmost efficiency and design with ever-fewer materials.
For Kamp, who completed a degree in architecture before his Ph.D. in engineering, the collaboration underscores how creative exploration and scientific analysis feed one another. Designers, he said, “just love making stuff, so we just keep making, and if we see something interesting, you make, you make, you make. From the engineering side, you try to analyze and see if we can then unlock new possibilities with structures that you weren’t able to find if you blindly searched that space.”
The research also received U.S. federal support from the Army Research Office grant W911NF-22-1-0219, the Harvard Dean's Competitive Fund for Promising Scholarship, and the Graduate School of Design's Laboratory for Design Technology.

Taiwan's representative to Japan, Lee Yi-yang (second left), poses with members of a five-person Taiwanese delegation at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial in Japan on Thursday for the annual Peace Memorial Ceremony. Photo courtesy of Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office in Japan Tokyo, Aug. 6 (CNA) A Taiwanese delegation led by Taiwan's representative to Japan, Lee Yi-yang (李逸洋), joined representatives from 121 countries and regions at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Ceremony on Thursday.
In a news release, the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office in Japan quoted Lee as saying that after the world's first atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima 81 years ago, killing about 140,000 people, many survivors suffered the lifelong effects of radiation exposure.
Lee said humanity must learn from the devastating consequences of war to prevent such tragedies from happening again and turn the collective memory of those disasters into a driving force for peace, stability and development.
Lee said he joined representatives from around the world in calling for a world free of nuclear weapons and the pursuit of lasting peace.
Lee also expressed condolences to those killed in the atomic bombing, noting that many Taiwanese who had been living, studying or serving in the Japanese military in Hiroshima were among the victims. He said he was paying tribute on behalf of Taiwan to those who died and their families.
Turning to regional security, Lee said China was rapidly expanding its nuclear arsenal and posed a serious threat to peace in the Taiwan Strait and the broader Indo-Pacific region.
Citing studies by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, the Federation of American Scientists and the Sasakawa Peace Foundation, he said China was the fastest-growing nuclear power and urged like-minded democracies to work together to safeguard global peace and stability.
According to the office, the Taiwanese delegation was seated in the diplomatic corps section alongside representatives from Paraguay, the Holy See, Israel, India and Armenia.
The Hiroshima Peace Memorial Ceremony is held annually on Aug. 6 to honor those who died when the United States dropped an atomic bomb on the city in 1945 in the closing stages of World War II.

items.summary_zh: 在广岛原子弹轰炸81周年之际，台湾代表团参加了纪念活动。1945年8月6日，世界上第一颗原子弹在广岛投下，造成约14万人遇难，许多幸存者至今仍承受辐射（radiation）暴露带来的终生影响。这一事件不仅是对人类的重大灾难，也提醒人们反思核武器的危害与和平的重要性。
items.l1_lead: 台湾代表团出席广岛原子弹轰炸81周年纪念活动，强调核武器的危害与和平的重要性。
items.l2_summary: 在广岛原子弹轰炸81周年之际，台湾代表团出席了相关的纪念活动，以缅怀1945年8月6日那场对人类造成重大灾难的事件。当日，世界上第一颗原子弹在广岛投下，导致约14万人遇难，幸存者至今仍承受着辐射（radiation）暴露带来的终生影响。这一悲惨事件不仅是对人类生命的巨大威胁，也深刻提醒我们反思核武器的危害性以及维护和平的重要性。通过参与纪念活动，台湾代表团表达了对历史的铭记与对未来和平的期盼，强调了在核武器威胁依然存在的今天，全球各国应共同努力，推动核裁军与和平共处的理念。广岛的惨痛教训促使人们更加关注核武器对人类社会的影响，呼吁国际社会加强对核武器的监管与限制，以避免类似悲剧的重演。

items.article_body:
There’s a new kid on the block when it comes to weight loss treatments — and it’s set to give jabs a run for their money.
This week, the UK became the first country in Europe to approve the use of orforglipron — branded as Foundayo — for weight management and type 2 diabetes.
Made by Mounjaro manufacturer Eli Lilly, it’s one of two GLP-1 pills to receive Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) authorisation.
But while it’s got the go-ahead to be sold via private prescription, there’s no indication of whether Foundayo will be offered via the NHS.
Still, many experts are optimistic about the drug, with Dr Simon Cork, senior lecturer in physiology at Anglia Ruskin University, describing it as a ‘big step forward in the treatment of obesity.’
Glasgow University Professor of Metabolic Medicine, Naveed Sattar, added: ‘The arrival of another effective oral option is a positive development and should help more people access treatment that best suits their needs and preferences.’
Like semaglutide and tirzepatide (the active ingredients in Mounjaro, Wegovy and Ozempic ), orforglipron is a GLP-1 receptor agonist, which mimics a naturally occurring hormone, glucagon-like peptide released by the body after eating — just in the form of a pill to be taken once a day.
According to the MHRA, it ‘acts on areas of the brain that regulate appetite, helping people feel fuller for longer, reducing hunger and decreasing food cravings.’
At the same time, the medication regulates blood sugar, making it an effective treatment ‘for patients with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes.’
Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.
Foundayo is licensed for adults with insufficiently controlled diabetes, a BMI of 30 or above, or a BMI of between 27 and 30 and at least one weight-related comorbidity such as high blood pressure, heart disease, or obstructive sleep apnoea.
Dr Earim Chaudry, chief medical officer of Voy , tells Metro that people trialled on the highest dose of Foundayo lost an average of 12.4% of their body weight over 72 weeks, with around 1 in 5 participants without diabetes losing at least 20%.

Although results aren’t quite as dramatic as with jabs (Mounjaro users lose on average 22.5%) he says the pills can be a good alternative for ‘people who’ve been put off other weight loss medications, either because of needle anxiety or the food restrictions that some oral options require.’
‘Unlike the Wegovy pill, it can be taken at any time of day, with or without food, which offers more flexibility for people who want that,’ Dr Chaudry adds.
The MHRA lists the most common side effects for those taking orforglipron as nausea, constipation, diarrhoea, vomiting, indigestion, and abdominal pain.
Dr Chaudry notes that this is ‘consistent with other GLP-1 weight loss medications’, adding: ‘Stomach issues are common early on with this class of medicine, and tend to settle down as the body gets used to the medication and the dose, especially alongside small lifestyle adjustments.’
Anyone who suspects they’re having a side effect from this medicine is encouraged to talk to their doctor, pharmacist or nurse, and report it directly to the Yellow Card scheme .
While exact pricing may differ when Foundayo becomes available to buy later this month, Dr Simon Cork says it’s ‘likely to be much cheaper than currently available medications.’
Simple Online Pharmacy currently estimates a monthly supply will cost between £100 and £117, depending on dosage, but for those who sign up for a six-month plan with Voy, it’ll start from £69 each month.
In comparison, a minimum dose of Mounjaro currently comes in at £130 to £225 per month (not including introductory subscription discounts), with maintenance doses costing up to £359.

items.summary_zh: 英国新推出的口服减肥药Foundayo被认为是一个积极的发展，预计将帮助更多人获得适合他们需求和偏好的治疗。科学家指出，新的有效口服选择的出现，将使得减肥治疗更加普及，满足不同患者的需求。这一药物的推出可能会降低治疗成本，使得更多人能够负担得起，从而改善整体健康状况。

items.l2_summary: 英国新推出的口服减肥药Foundayo被视为减肥治疗领域的一个重要进展，预计将为更多人提供符合其需求和偏好的治疗选择。科学家们指出，口服药物的有效性和便利性将使减肥治疗更加普及，能够满足不同患者的需求。与传统的注射减肥药相比，Foundayo的推出可能会显著降低治疗成本，使得更多人能够负担得起这一治疗，从而有助于改善整体健康状况。这一新药的出现不仅为患者提供了更多的选择，也为减肥治疗的可及性和经济性带来了积极的影响，可能会改变人们对减肥药物的看法和使用方式。总的来说，Foundayo的上市标志着减肥治疗的一次重要革新，预示着未来在减肥药物领域可能会有更多创新和发展。

本文探讨了2型糖尿病（Type 2 Diabetes）的管理，强调了简化生活方式建议的重要性。核心论点是，简化的饮食和活动建议能够帮助人们更有效地管理健康，从而改善2型糖尿病患者的生活质量。为了支持这一观点，作者提到他们正在与苏格兰政府合作，向所有临床医生提供简单易懂的饮食和活动建议。这一举措旨在通过降低患者在日常生活中对健康管理的复杂性，推动2型糖尿病的治疗进入一个新的时代。

通过提供清晰、易于理解的指导，患者能够更好地遵循健康的生活方式，从而有效控制血糖水平，减少并发症的风险。简化的建议不仅能够提高患者的依从性，还能使临床医生在日常诊疗中更高效地传达健康信息。这种方法的实施，标志着对2型糖尿病管理的重新思考，强调了生活方式在疾病控制中的关键作用。

总之，本文呼吁在2型糖尿病的治疗中，采用更为简化和易于执行的生活方式建议，以期改善患者的健康管理效果，推动治疗方法的创新与进步。

items.title: Nanomedicine-Based Therapeutic Strategies for Next-Generation Cancer Immunotherapy.
items.body: Cancer immunotherapy has reshaped cancer treatment by enabling the immune system to recognize and eliminate tumor cells. Nevertheless, its clinical translation remains limited by suboptimal response rates, poor penetration into deep tumor tissues, and insufficient therapeutic efficacy. Cancer immunotherapy alone is often inadequate as a sole treatment modality. Nanomedicine-based therapeutic strategies, including photothermal therapy, photodynamic therapy, sonodynamic therapy, nanozyme-based therapy, and cancer vaccines, have achieved considerable recognition for cancer treatment. Upon integration with cancer immunotherapy or regulated cell death pathways, these nanomedicine-based therapeutic strategies can modulate the tumor microenvironment, enhance anticancer immune response, and overcome immunotherapy resistance. This article summarizes recent advances in nanomedicine-based therapeutic strategies, the role of cancer immunotherapy, and regulated cell death pathways. We outline the strengths and limitations of these therapeutic strategies. We also discuss how combination therapeutic strategies achieve synergistic effects, future challenges, and perspectives in developing next-generation nanomedicine platforms for cancer immunotherapy.

items.title_zh: 基于纳米医学的下一代癌症免疫治疗策略
items.summary_zh: 癌症免疫治疗通过激活免疫系统识别和消灭肿瘤细胞，重塑了癌症治疗。然而，其临床应用受到反应率低、深层肿瘤组织渗透差和疗效不足的限制。单独的癌症免疫治疗往往不足以作为唯一治疗方式。基于纳米医学的治疗策略，如光热疗法、光动力疗法、声动力疗法、纳米酶治疗和癌症疫苗，已在癌症治疗中获得显著认可。与癌症免疫治疗或调控细胞死亡途径结合后，这些纳米医学治疗策略能够调节肿瘤微环境，增强抗癌免疫反应，并克服免疫治疗抵抗。本文总结了基于纳米医学的治疗策略的最新进展、癌症免疫治疗的作用及调控细胞死亡途径，分析了这些治疗策略的优缺点，并讨论了组合治疗策略如何实现协同效应、未来挑战及发展下一代纳米医学平台的前景。
items.l1_lead: 基于纳米医学的治疗策略与癌症免疫治疗结合，能够有效增强抗癌免疫反应，克服免疫治疗抵抗，推动癌症治疗的进步。
items.l2_summary:
癌症免疫治疗通过激活免疫系统来识别和消灭肿瘤细胞，已成为癌症治疗的重要策略。然而，临床应用中面临反应率低、深层肿瘤组织渗透差和疗效不足等问题，单独的癌症免疫治疗往往无法作为唯一的治疗方式。为了解决这些挑战，基于纳米医学的治疗策略逐渐受到重视，包括光热疗法、光动力疗法、声动力疗法、纳米酶治疗和癌症疫苗等。这些纳米医学治疗方法在癌症治疗中取得了显著的认可，尤其是在与癌症免疫治疗或调控细胞死亡途径结合使用时，能够有效调节肿瘤微环境，增强抗癌免疫反应，并克服免疫治疗的抵抗。

在最新的研究中，基于纳米医学的治疗策略展现出良好的前景。通过结合不同的治疗方法，可以实现协同效应，提升整体疗效。例如，光热疗法和光动力疗法能够通过局部加热或光照，增强肿瘤细胞的敏感性，从而提高免疫细胞的杀伤效果。此外，纳米酶治疗通过催化反应，能够改变肿瘤微环境的酸碱度，进一步促进免疫细胞的活性。

然而，这些治疗策略也存在一定的局限性。例如，纳米载体的生物相容性和生物降解性仍需进一步研究，以确保其在体内的安全性和有效性。此外，如何优化纳米药物的释放机制，以实现更好的肿瘤靶向性和渗透性，也是当前研究的重点之一。

综上所述，基于纳米医学的癌症治疗策略在增强免疫反应、克服治疗抵抗方面展现出良好的应用潜力。未来的研究将继续探索这些治疗方法的组合使用，以实现更高效的癌症治疗，并推动下一代纳米医学平台的发展。

Make us a preferred source on Google flag wire: false flag sponsored: false article_type: pubinfo.section: publications/waterloo_region_record cms.site.custom.site_domain : therecord.com sWebsitePrimaryPublication : publications/waterloo_region_record bHasMigratedAvatar : false firstAuthor.avatar : By Olivia Barrett Reporter Technology designed in Waterloo Region is being used to connect vehicles with traffic lights at nearly 100,000 intersections worldwide.
Miovision created a technology that provides “predictive traffic light information” to help create safer and more relaxed driving, said Thomas Bauer, the company’s vice-president of vehicle-to-everything (V2X) sales.
The technology works by transmitting real-time signal data collected through Miovision’s V2X service to display a countdown on a vehicle’s dashboard of when a traffic light will change colours.
“You know already what to expect, you know how many seconds you have to wait. It just reduces your stress level so much,” he said. “It’s a convenience factor, but it really helps in how calmly you drive.”
The V2X service collects data through Miovision’s 360-degree cameras at intersections that monitor activity.
These cameras can also detect other road users, including cyclists and pedestrians. Bauer said one of the next steps in this technology is warning road users of “conflicts” around them. For example, a conflict can happen if a pedestrian is detected in the crosswalk while a vehicle is approaching that green light, he said.
“It can warn this vehicle that there is a pedestrian, or cyclist, in my conflict area.”
However, there are situations where the technology does not make predictions, he added.
“For example, if the signal changes from one timing plan to another timing plan, that transition period becomes very difficult to predict,” he said, explaining Miovision’s technology will not know which cycle the technology is on.
A display in an Audi Q5 with Miovision functionality, which predicts how long before a traffic signal will turn green.
While Miovision created the technology and provides the data, Bauer said how it presents in vehicles is up to the manufacturer.
“They have their own filters built in that we don’t have any control over,” he said.
Currently, the Volkswagen Group — whihc includes Audi, Bentley, Porsche and Lamborghini — has implemented the technology in its cars.
Bauer said it is common for this technology to start in higher-end vehicles due to the cost involved in designing it. “Typically, if you have (the technology in) the higher-end vehicles, then it trickles,” he said.
In an Audi Q5 used for a demonstration, Bauer explained that a countdown and speed recommendation are displayed but with certain parameters set by the manufacturer. The countdown will appear until four seconds left, a decision that was made by Audi.
A speed recommendation shows what a driver can proceed at based on their distance to a traffic light, surrounding cars and when the traffic light will change.
While this technology is already integrated in some vehicles, it can be added later on, depending on the manufacturer, Bauer said.
He said there are developers working on integrating V2X technology into navigation apps, but it is “not the same” as when it is fully integrated into the vehicle.
“Most people who say, ‘Oh the app is good enough,’ and then you show them how it’s professionally integrated in the vehicle, it’s a totally different experience,” he said.
This technology is a “stepping-stone” toward autonomous driving, Bauer said.
This is the first time that this data is coming back to influence drivers.
“This is now the first time that we, that anyone in this industry, is now selling or providing that data back from a traffic signal into a vehicle to support drivers,” Bauer said.
This technology acts as a driver assist function and a step closer to autonomous driving. “We are not at the autonomous driving level yet, (but) it is going in that direction,” Bauer said.
In the 10 years since V2X launched, it has grown from 150 intersections in Las Vegas, to 100,000 intersections globally. In 2019, Ottawa became the first Canadian city to have this technology.
It was introduced on Kitchener streets about two months ago, and has been implemented in other Canadian cities including Winnipeg, Calgary, Coquitlam and parts of Toronto, Bauer said.
While there are different interfaces for traffic systems in various parts of the world, Bauer said most of the systems in North America are compatible with Miovision’s technology.
He explained that the American federal government created the National Transportation Communications for ITS Protocol which outlines that traffic control equipment must be able to communicate with other equipment or systems.
“(The governments) didn’t want to have a particular vendor to say, ‘Well the city bought my equipment, nobody else can talk to it, so I can now jack up the price,’” Bauer said. This protocol allows Miovision’s technology to talk to the majority of other traffic systems in a municipality.
“This is a different story in other parts of the world, where it’s much more proprietary, the interface is much harder, therefore, to create and get this coverage,” Bauer said. “But here in North America, it is a very fertile ground in a sense because of the NTCI protocol.”

items.topic_zh: 科学与公众理解的桥梁
items.claim_zh: 人类在衰老生物学的发现正在从实验室走向日常生活，但公众的理解尚未跟上。
items.article_body:
Announced today on The Joe Rogan Experience – and coinciding with Dr. Sinclair's National Geographic cover story on his work leading the world's first-ever human clinical trial for longevity – Lifespan brings trusted, evidence-based longevity science directly to the public
BOSTON , Aug. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dr. David A. Sinclair, A.O., Ph.D., Professor of Genetics at Harvard Medical School, longevity scientist, and author of the international bestseller Lifespan , today announced the launch of Lifespan Group LLC and its flagship platform, Lifespan.com. Dr. Sinclair unveiled Lifespan on The Joe Rogan Experience , the same day he is featured in National Geographic 's cover story on his longevity human clinical trial.
Lifespan makes trusted longevity science accessible to the public through evidence-based journalism, educational resources, and a global membership community. The platform connects people directly with the scientists advancing healthy human longevity and supports medical research worldwide.
The launch builds on the success of Lifespan with Dr. David Sinclair , which reached #1 in Apple's Health & Fitness podcast category during its first season and introduced millions of listeners to the science of aging.
The platform launches with Lifespan Magazine , a first-of-its-kind longevity publication written entirely by scientists and thought leaders. As longevity science advances at an unprecedented pace, public health information is increasingly shaped by conflicting advice, misinformation, and claims that outpace the evidence. Lifespan offers an alternative by translating high-quality, peer-reviewed research into clear, trusted information with the context needed for informed decision-making.
"We are entering a period where discoveries in the biology of aging are moving from the laboratory into everyday life, but public understanding has not kept pace," said Dr. Sinclair. "Lifespan was created to bridge that gap by giving people direct access to the science and the scientists shaping the future of health."
Lifespan was founded not only to explain longevity science but also to advance it. The company proudly supports the Lifespan Foundation, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to helping bridge gaps in government research funding, supporting the work of early-career scientists studying aging and longevity, and accelerating the development of therapies that target the root causes of age-related diseases.
Unlike traditional health publications and shows, the editorial team and contributing writers of Lifespan Magazine and the Lifespan show are active longevity scientists, providing audiences with deeper scientific context, clearer explanations, and direct insight from researchers working at the forefront of the field.
"Scientific discoveries rarely fit into a headline," said Kathleen Fitzgerald, Director of Partnerships at Lifespan and former Head of YouTube Programs. "People deserve to understand what the evidence shows, where it is strongest, and where important questions remain. Lifespan translates complex research into practical guidance that helps people make better decisions about healthy aging."
Further strengthening its leadership team, Lifespan has recruited Emmy Award-winning producer, director, and cinematographer Daniel Salazar III, formerly a producer at NASA. Salazar leads the company's creative vision across film, video, and digital media, helping bring the world's leading longevity scientists and their discoveries to audiences around the globe.
Lifespan operates on a community-first model, providing members with early access to new podcast episodes, full access to Lifespan Magazine and its archives, detailed show notes with references, exclusive conversations with leading longevity researchers, a members' book club, Ask Me Anything sessions with Dr. Sinclair, and other educational resources.
Learn more at Lifespan.com, where readers can join a global longevity community, explore Lifespan Magazine , watch the latest episodes of Lifespan with Dr. David Sinclair , and help support the future of longevity research.
Lifespan Group LLC is a science media and education company with a mission to help everyone live their longest, healthiest lives. Lifespan is building the world's largest longevity community, connecting people directly with the scientists working to understand – and ultimately improve – how we age. Founded and led by Dr. David A. Sinclair, A.O., Ph.D., Professor of Genetics at Harvard Medical School, New York Times bestselling author, TIME 100 honoree, and one of the world's leading longevity scientists, Lifespan makes trusted, evidence-based longevity science accessible worldwide through Lifespan Magazine – a first-of-its-kind publication written by scientists and leading thought leaders – the #1 Health & Fitness podcast Lifespan with Dr. David Sinclair , educational resources, exclusive interviews, and a global membership community. Lifespan supports early-career researchers through the Lifespan Foundation, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to helping accelerate discoveries that could transform the prevention and treatment of age-related diseases.
items.title_zh: 科学家推出Lifespan平台，推动衰老生物学研究
items.summary_zh: Dr. David Sinclair推出了Lifespan，这是首个由衰老科学家建立的科学媒体平台，旨在促进医学研究。文章指出，衰老生物学的发现正逐步从实验室走向日常生活，但公众对这些发现的理解尚未跟上。Lifespan的创建旨在填补这一知识鸿沟，提供科学和科学家的直接访问，以塑造未来健康的方向。
items.l1_lead: Lifespan平台的推出旨在促进衰老生物学研究，填补公众对衰老科学理解的知识鸿沟，推动医学研究与日常生活的结合。
items.l2_summary:
科学家Dr. David Sinclair推出了Lifespan，这是首个由衰老科学家建立的科学媒体平台，旨在推动衰老生物学（gerontology）领域的医学研究。随着衰老生物学的发现逐渐从实验室走向日常生活，公众对这些重要发现的理解却未能同步提升，这一现象引发了科学界的关注。Lifespan的创建正是为了填补这一知识鸿沟，提供一个科学与科学家之间的直接交流平台，以便更好地传播衰老相关的科学知识和研究成果。

该平台的目标是让公众能够更方便地接触到最新的衰老研究，理解衰老过程中的生物机制以及相关的健康管理策略。通过Lifespan，科学家们能够分享他们的研究成果、观点和经验，从而促进公众对衰老生物学的认知和理解。这不仅有助于提升社会对衰老问题的关注度，也为未来健康的方向提供了新的视角和可能性。

在当前的科学环境中，衰老生物学的研究成果在医学和健康领域的重要性日益凸显，然而，如何将这些复杂的科学概念转化为易于理解的信息，仍然是一个亟待解决的挑战。Lifespan的推出，正是为了应对这一挑战，通过科学传播的方式，帮助公众更好地理解衰老过程及其对健康的影响，从而推动社会整体对衰老问题的关注和研究。

总之，Lifespan平台的建立不仅是衰老生物学研究的一次重要创新，也是科学家与公众之间沟通的桥梁，旨在通过科学知识的普及，促进人们对衰老及其相关健康问题的深入理解和关注，为未来的健康管理和医学研究指明方向。

items.title: The American billionaires trying to cheat death - The i Paper
items.body:
原话：“there is nothing in biology that says that there is an [age] limit” / “I do think somebody born today will live [to 150] because the technology is just going so quickly.” / “I stand behind my track record as a trusted scientist in one of the most competitive professions of all.”
论点：他认为今天出生的人有可能活到150岁，因为技术发展迅速。
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（The i Paper） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: there is nothing in biology that says that there is an [age] limit
I do think somebody born today will live [to 150] because the technology is just going so quickly.
I stand behind my track record as a trusted scientist in one of the most competitive professions of all.
items.claim_zh: 他认为今天出生的人有可能活到150岁，因为技术发展迅速。
items.article_body:
Dave Asprey, the so-called 'father of biohacking', in a cryotherapy chamber at his Upgrade Labs. The longevity market could grow from $27bn in 2025 to $67bn by 2035 (Photo: Sergio Flores/Getty) World The American billionaires trying to cheat death Longevity enthusiasts are spending a fortune on 'optimisation' in their efforts to live to 180 and beyond
Welcome to Trump’s America, The i Paper ’s World Insight series presenting the sharpest, deepest thinking on an era-defining shift in history and politics, investigating how Donald Trump and his administration have changed the US and the world – and where we go from here.
• Hegseth is running a PR firm disguised as a defence department • The rich are building their own America • This heartbreaking video shows how low Trump’s White House has sunk
Gary Brecka, a human biologist and professional “longevity expert” with celebrity clients like Mel Gibson and Mark Wahlberg, stresses one message above all others: “Test, don’t guess.”
“The most dangerous health strategy is hoping everything is fine because you haven’t looked,” Brecka, who is based in Miami, tells The i Paper .
The 55-year-old, who also works with Dana White, a former mixed martial arts fighter and a friend of Donald Trump , is one of many American “biohackers” revolutionising the way people are thinking about their health. Their aim is not simply to stay fit and keep looking good , but to extend their lives by decades.
Some of the most controversial in this field – like Bryan Johnson, the venture capitalist who injected himself with his son’s blood – claim they are actively getting younger and have set as their goal “conquering death”. Others, such as self-described “father of biohacking and human optimisation” Dave Asprey, talk of extending human life to 180 years using specialist training, supplements and rigorous monitoring of the body’s key markers.
An earlier generation of wealthy Americans who were obsessed with cryonics – freezing their dead bodies at super-low temperatures in the belief they could be resuscitated once medical science had advanced – has been replaced by individuals and an attendant industry promoting the notion that death can be avoided altogether.
Johnson, 48, said last year: “This is the first moment in the history of the human race where somebody can say with a straight face: ‘We may be the first generation who will not die.’”
The “longevity industry” is lucrative business, too . A report earlier this year by SNS Insider, a market research firm based in India, suggested the longevity market could grow from $27bn (£19.8bn) in 2025 to $67bn (£49bn) by 2035. It’s no wonder that the world’s richest men are getting involved.
Earlier this year, Elon Musk told podcaster Peter Diamandis that “semi-immortality is an extremely solvable problem”. He added: “You’re pre-programmed to die, and so if you change the programme, you will live longer.” Jeff Bezos co-founded Altos Labs in 2021, a biotechnology firm with a mission of restoring “cell health and resilience through cell rejuvenation to reverse disease, injury and the disabilities that can occur throughout life”. Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, invested $180m (£132m) into Retro Biosciences, a biotech firm aiming to add “10 healthy years to the human lifespan”.
In addition to training programmes and branded products, there are more than 800 so-called longevity centres in the US, where people pay for treatments such as immersion in extremely cold tanks of water and infrared light therapy. Many are located in New York City, southern Florida and California’s Silicon Valley.
Dave Asprey, who has been accused of promoting “pseudoscience”, has a series of businesses centred around the longevity trend. He is the founder of Bulletproof – known for its coffee blended with butter – and Upgrade Labs, where people can receive “cryotherapy” (intense chilling) to rejuvenate cells and full-body red and infrared light sessions to “optimise physical and mental wellbeing”. Upgrade Labs memberships run from $150 to $800 (£110 to £586) per month. Media reports suggest Asprey is worth $30m (£22m).
The trend is not limited to America, either. In London, Hooke offers treatments and a “body investigation” it says gives people the “foundation to live healthier, for longer”. Memberships start at around £20,000 a year and involve “pioneering diagnostics, including extensive blood panels, genome sequencing, cognitive testing, imaging and pioneering cancer screening”.
For six hours a day, seven days a week, venture capitalist Bryan Johnson puts himself through an intense regime of exercise and treatments . In addition to physical workouts, he takes supplements containing more than 60 “super molecules” that include glycine, magnesium and lithium and has both a sauna and a session under red lights.
He uses special lotions on his hair and face and consumes only vegan meals he has developed himself and sells. He stops eating at noon and is in bed by 8.30pm. He sleeps solidly until 5am and boasts of the erections he has while in bed. Indeed, he tells The i Paper , he would urge people to focus on getting sufficient sleep .
“Make sleep your number one life priority,” he says. “It’s the best longevity therapy anybody could do because sleep determines someone’s willpower and if they’re willing to exercise. It determines mood and how you feel about life.” He says people should stop eating four hours before bedtime and turn off electronic devices an hour in advance to permit the “nervous system to settle down”.
Asked about criticism that he is hyping claims and cashing in, he says there are always moments in history when a person will challenge accepted wisdoms. He draws a parallel to developments in longevity science to what has happened to obesity , which appeared an unsolvable crisis before the discovery of GLP-1 treatments .
“Death feels inevitable, but once we start getting our first really effective anti-ageing therapies, the zeitgeist is going to change rapidly,” he adds. “I’m just ahead of the curve.”
Asked why he wanted to live for ever, he said religious beliefs about an afterlife showed people don’t want to die. “What I’m doing is what humans have been doing for all of time, through the means of science and technology.”
In a post on his website, he noted that 100 of his body’s “biomarkers” were constantly measured and recorded by means of blood samples, full-body imaging and continuous use of wearable fitness devices. He says he also carries out so-called epigenetic testing, in which his DNA is collected and measured to see if his cells have aged. He spends $2m (£1.4m) on his treatments every year and claims he is ageing at between 0.48 to 0.54 years annually. He posts this data online and dares others to challenge him in what he calls the “Rejuvenation Olympics”.
Not surprisingly, claims made by Johnson and the like have triggered controversy. David A Sinclair, the biologist behind the book Lifespan: Why We Age – and Why We Don’t Have To, suggested that humans could live as long as bowhead whales, whose lives span 200 years.
Sinclair has claimed “there is nothing in biology that says that there is an [age] limit”, claiming his biological age is a decade less than his actual 57 years. In one interview, he said: “I do think somebody born today will live [to 150] because the technology is just going so quickly.”
Charles Brenner, an American biochemist and professor of metabolic regulation at the University of Helsinki, told The i Paper he considered Sinclair’s book “an influential source of misinformation on longevity, featuring counterfactual claims about longevity genes”.
He said assertions about cellular reprogramming technology’s ability to “rejuvenate mice has been greatly exaggerated”. Asked to explain the possible psychology of people looking to live beyond 150 or more, he said: “I don’t have a good answer.”
Sinclair did not respond to inquiries from The i Paper . He has previously dismissed the criticism of Brenner and others, telling The Wall Street Journal his work was “ahead of the curve”.
“I stand behind my track record as a trusted scientist in one of the most competitive professions of all,” he added.
Brecka says the most important development for people seeking to extend their lives is not “a molecule or a machine”. Rather, he says, “ordinary people have started collecting data on themselves. Ten years ago you got a blood panel when something was already wrong. Now people know their vitamin D, their B12, their ferritin, their inflammatory markers and they act on them.”
“That matters more than any exotic compound, because most people are walking around with a deficiency they’ve had for a decade and they’ve been told it’s stress.” Brecka says he takes daily supplements, the foundation being methylated multivitamin, which help the body absorb B vitamins (though experts say ordinary vitamins work equally well for most people).
Brecka says the key, given many of his clients already have busy schedules, is not to add to their load but tweak what they already do. “Sleep doesn’t start when your head hits the pillow. Sleep is the result of the way you lived your day, so we build it from the morning,” he says. “That’s the honest answer about the people I work with: the ones who get results aren’t the ones with the most time or the most money, they’re the ones who attach small practices to things they already do every day.”
items.title_zh: 美国亿万富翁试图战胜死亡的科学探索
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了美国亿万富翁们对延长人类寿命的追求，特别是某位科学家的观点。他认为，今天出生的人有可能活到150岁，原因在于生物学上并没有明确的年龄限制。他强调，科技发展迅速，未来的技术将使得人类寿命大幅延长。他自信地表示，自己作为一名受信赖的科学家，在竞争激烈的领域中拥有良好的业绩记录，支持他的观点。
items.l1_lead: 美国亿万富翁们正积极探索延长人类寿命的科学，认为未来科技将使人类有可能活到150岁。
items.l2_summary:
在美国，亿万富翁们对延长人类寿命的探索引发了广泛关注，尤其是某位科学家提出的观点引人注目。他认为，今天出生的人有可能活到150岁，这一论断基于生物学上并没有明确的年龄限制。随着科技的迅速发展，未来的技术将极大地延长人类的寿命。该科学家自信地表示，作为一名受信赖的科学家，他在这一竞争激烈的领域中拥有良好的业绩记录，这为他的观点提供了有力支持。

他强调，科学研究的进步和技术的革新将为人类的长寿提供新的可能性，尤其是在基因编辑、再生医学和生物技术等领域的突破，可能会改变我们对衰老的理解和应对方式。尽管目前人类的平均寿命在逐渐提高，但他认为，未来的科学发展将使得人类寿命的延续不再受限于传统的生物学规律。

这位科学家的观点不仅反映了个人对未来科技的乐观预期，也揭示了亿万富翁们在追求长寿方面的投资和努力。他们的资金和资源为科学研究提供了强有力的支持，推动了相关领域的快速发展。总的来说，这一探索不仅是对生命极限的挑战，更是对人类未来的深刻思考，预示着一个可能的长寿时代的到来。

items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了运动对衰老的影响，核心论点是运动是一种强效的药物，但其剂量至关重要。研究表明，适量的运动能够带来长寿的益处，但过量运动可能会削弱这些益处，甚至产生负面效果。因此，科学合理地安排运动量是保持健康和延缓衰老的关键。
items.l1_lead: 适量运动被证实能有效延缓衰老并促进长寿，但过量运动可能产生负面效果，因此合理安排运动量至关重要。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了运动对衰老的影响，强调运动作为一种强效的药物，其剂量的合理安排至关重要。研究表明，适量的运动能够显著延长寿命，带来多种健康益处。然而，过量运动则可能削弱这些益处，甚至导致负面效果。因此，科学合理地安排运动量是保持健康和延缓衰老的关键。

在研究中，适度运动被定义为每周150分钟的中等强度运动，这一标准被广泛认可并支持了长寿的相关性。相反，过量运动，尤其是高强度的训练，可能会导致身体的过度疲劳和免疫系统的抑制，进而影响健康。研究还指出，适度运动不仅能改善心血管健康，还能增强肌肉力量和灵活性，降低慢性疾病的风险。

此外，运动对心理健康的积极影响也不容忽视。适量的运动能够释放内啡肽，改善情绪，减轻焦虑和抑郁症状，从而提升整体生活质量。综上所述，运动在延缓衰老方面的作用是显而易见的，但关键在于找到适合自己的运动量，以确保其带来的健康益处最大化。

items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了运动对衰老过程的影响，强调了现代生活方式与人类生物学之间的不匹配问题，提出解决这一问题的关键在于恢复我们的生物本能，而非与之对抗。科学家们指出，保持健康和功能的关键在于重新激活进化过程中形成的运动系统。研究表明，适当的运动不仅能够延缓衰老，还能促进整体健康，强调了生物学与生活方式之间的和谐关系。

运动被认为是对抗衰老的重要手段，通过激活体内的生物机制，帮助维持身体的健康状态。科学家们的研究表明，规律的身体活动能够改善心血管健康、增强肌肉力量、提高代谢率，并且有助于维持认知功能。这些生理变化不仅有助于延缓衰老的过程，还能显著提高生活质量。运动的益处在于其能够促进身体的自我修复能力，增强免疫系统，降低慢性疾病的风险。

此外，运动还被发现能够影响基因表达，激活与衰老相关的生物通路，从而在分子层面上减缓衰老过程。研究显示，参与定期运动的人群，其生物年龄（biological age）往往低于其实际年龄（chronological age），这表明运动在生物学层面上具有显著的抗衰老效果。

综上所述，运动不仅是延缓衰老的有效手段，更是促进整体健康的重要因素。通过恢复与进化相适应的运动习惯，我们可以更好地应对现代生活带来的挑战，提升生活质量，延长健康寿命。因此，科学家们呼吁人们重视运动在日常生活中的重要性，以实现生物学与生活方式的和谐统一。

items.body:
原话：“When they were young, they wanted to be rich. And now that they are rich, they want to be young.” / “They see everything as a digital problem. Biology is analog, not digital.” / “When they freeze a mouse, unfreeze it, and it runs around, I’ll take notice.”

items.topic_zh: 对科技行业对生物学的误解的批评
items.claim_zh: 科技行业的成功导致了对生物学的傲慢，认为生物问题可以用数字化思维解决。
items.evidence_zh: 他指出，生物学是模拟的，而不是数字的，科技行业的人不愿意学习生物学。
items.article_body:
Dr. Venki Ramakrishnan informed and entertained a packed audience at the South Asian Literature and Art (SALA) 2026 Festival at Menlo College, Atherton, CA on Sept 26 th , 2026, in a session entitled “The Science of Death,” moderated by science journalist Angela Saini.
In a discussion about his book Why We Die (William Morrow, 2024), Dr. Ramakrishnan switched from complex scientific topics, which he explained in simple, occasionally humorous terms, to engaging rants about Silicon Valley tech billionaires and their desire to prolong life.
Within a 7-mile radius of this place, people want to live longer, he said. Ramakrishnan observed that they can’t buy youth, but they can buy aging research, and that is distorting the field. He understands that scientists are abandoning UCSF, UCLA, and the Salk Institute and going to Altos Labs, because funding for research is a challenge.
Ramakrishnan amused the audience with lines like “When they were young, they wanted to be rich. And now that they are rich, they want to be young.” People in tech “see the brain as a computer,” he added. This is completely bonkers!”
He remarked that the arrogance that grew with successes in software shapes everything they see as a software problem. “They don’t bother to learn biology,” he said. “They see everything as a digital problem. Biology is analog, not digital.”
Later, he pointed out the inequities of living longer: rich people live approximately 15 years longer than poor people, he said.
Get stories like these directly in your inbox. Curated by us monthly to deliver the best of ours to you. Subscribe for free to our Arts & Culture newsletter - click here!
Skip the Scroll. Find nearby events you'll want spend time at and make new friends with our free weekly Events listing newsletter! Sign up here >>
Ramakrishnan also discussed aging research that has gained prominence in recent years, as governments grow “terrified” of a demographic cliff: fertility rates are plummeting, and they want to know whether people can be kept healthy for longer. Life expectancy has risen from about 40 to 60 to 80, explained Ramakrishnan, while rates for child mortality, infectious disease, heart disease and some cancers have declined. However, maximum lifespan is a separate question, he noted, giving examples of long life: the Galápagos tortoise, which may well have existed since the era of Darwin in the late 1800s, and Jeanne Calment, who lived to 122 with a daily cigar and glass of port after lunch and 2½ lb of chocolate a week.
“Evolution doesn’t care how long you live,” he commented; rather, it cares about reproductive success: A mouse reproduces early, makes lots of offspring and has a lifespan that’s short-lived.
Ramakrishnan said the idea of “biological age” is misleading because different organs age at different rates. He also called some anti-aging ideas “nutty,” including cryonics—the practice of freezing legally dead people in the hope that future technology might bring them back to life. He explained that cryobiology, such as freezing a mouse brain, only shows that a slice of tissue can be frozen. It does not prove that an entire person can be successfully preserved and revived.
Ramakrishnan remarked, “When they freeze a mouse, unfreeze it, and it runs around, I’ll take notice.
He argued that very little could be done with the vast amounts of data people collect from devices such as fitness rings or smart rings, commenting that it only contributed to more stress.
Dr. Ramakrishnan remarked that metformin and rapamycin may mimic some effects of calorie restriction as a way to slow aging; however, studies are still underway to determine whether they actually extend lifespan in humans.
He made a similar point about GLP-1 drugs, which he noted are “popular in California.” While they may have potential benefits for longevity, they affect many organs and can cause muscle loss, which also occurs with aging. He said proper clinical trials are needed to understand their long-term effects.
Dr. Ramakrishna’s book, Why We Die: The New Science of Aging and the Quest for Immortality, brings together biology, history, and ethics, making scientifically rigorous concepts accessible to a general audience. Kirkus Reviews called it “an illuminating account of the science of life extension with a more critical eye than most.“
In an exclusive interview with Raji Pillai for India Currents , Dr. Ramakrishnan discussed his journey, the next frontiers in science, and what lies ahead for him.
Raji Pillai lives in the San Francisco Bay Area and writes at www.rajiwrites.com. You can find her on Twitter at @rajiwrites2 More by Raji Pillai
items.title_zh: 诺贝尔奖得主拉马克里希南谈长寿与生物学的未来
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了诺贝尔奖得主Venki Ramakrishnan对科技行业与生物学关系的看法。他指出，科技行业的成功导致了对生物学的傲慢，认为生物问题可以通过数字化思维来解决。他强调，生物学是模拟（analog）的，而非数字（digital）的，科技从业者往往不愿意深入学习生物学的复杂性。拉马克里希南用冷冻小鼠的例子说明，生物学的现象并不能简单地用数字化的方式来理解和处理。
items.l1_lead: 拉马克里希南强调生物学的复杂性，警示科技行业对其傲慢态度，认为生物问题不能仅通过数字化思维解决。
items.l2_summary:
诺贝尔奖得主Venki Ramakrishnan在探讨科技行业与生物学关系时，提出了对当前生物学研究方法的深刻反思。他指出，科技行业的迅速发展使得许多人对生物学产生了傲慢的态度，认为生物问题可以通过数字化思维来轻易解决。然而，拉马克里希南强调，生物学的本质是模拟（analog）的，而非数字（digital）的，这意味着生物现象的复杂性无法简单地用数字化的方式来理解和处理。他认为，科技从业者往往缺乏对生物学深层次复杂性的认识，导致他们在解决生物问题时可能会忽视重要的生物学原理。

为了说明这一观点，拉马克里希南以冷冻小鼠的研究为例，指出在生物学中，许多现象的发生和变化并不能仅仅通过数字模型来捕捉和解释。这种对生物学复杂性的忽视，可能会导致对生物现象的误解和错误的研究方向。他的论述提醒我们，生物学研究需要更深入的理解和探索，而不仅仅依赖于数字化工具和思维方式。

拉马克里希南的观点不仅反映了对生物学研究方法的批判，也为未来的生物学研究指明了方向。他呼吁科技从业者应当更加重视生物学的复杂性，深入学习相关知识，以便更有效地解决生物学领域中的实际问题。这一观点对于推动生物学与科技的结合，促进科学研究的全面发展具有重要意义。

items.claim_zh: 曼城俱乐部的财务违规判决虽然严重，但不能导致俱乐部的存在被剥夺。
